findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler left abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: In src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py line 11, MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but implements nothing (pass). StatefulDetectorHandler has abstractmethods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data, so the subclass remains abstract. Detector.detector_handler does group_type.detector_handler(self) with no try/except, so accessing the handler for type metric_alert_fire will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class. Consequence: any detector of that type crashes process_detectors and blocks other detectors in the same batch, whereas before it returned [].

findings.title: get_state_data KeyErrors when counter_names is empty
findings.body: In src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py line 222, get_state_data initializes counter_updates={} and only populates it inside if self.counter_names:. It then unconditionally does counter_updates[gk] when building DetectorStateData. If a StatefulDetectorHandler defines counter_names=[] (valid for a detector with no counters), the guard is falsy, the dict stays empty, and every lookup raises KeyError. Consequence: any counter-less stateful detector crashes on every evaluate call.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says returns a list
findings.body: In src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py line 230, StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the signature and implementation in this PR return dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]. Consequence: readers and future implementers are misled about the contract.

findings.title: Test builds expected occurrence with wrong group_key
findings.body: In tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py line 537, TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds occurrence via build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...) whose fingerprint is derived from "val1", but the expected DetectorEvaluationResult and the actual evaluate_group_key_value call use group_key "group_key". Since fingerprint includes group_key, expected vs actual IssueOccurrence differ, so the equality assertion is wrong. Consequence: the test fails or does not actually validate the dedupe path it claims to cover.
